mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing liquidity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not positively correlated with low FEDFUNDS levels, or if the Rank IC falls below 0.03 in out-of-sample testing.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate signals labor market weakness, which can lead to decreased consumer spending and negative impacts on corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns following a significant rise in UNRATE, or if the mechanism fails to predict negative returns in more than 40% of cases during economic slowdowns.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) is strong but the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is simultaneously high, it indicates inefficiencies in the labor market that may signal broader economic weaknesses, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns despite strong PAYEMS growth coupled with high UNRATE, or if the Rank IC for this mechanism is below 0.05 in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) reflects strong economic activity and corporate earnings potential, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns following an increase in INDPRO, or if the mechanism fails to predict positive returns in more than 40% of cases during economic expansions.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 0.5% indicates monetary tightening, which can increase borrowing costs and reduce liquidity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns after FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.5%, or if the Rank IC for this mechanism is below 0.03 in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates strong aggregate demand, which is positively correlated with corporate earnings and equity market performance, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns following GDP growth, or if the mechanism fails to predict positive returns in more than 40% of cases during expansions.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of housing starts (HOUST) in a late-cycle expansion may indicate overbuilding, leading to future corrections in the housing market and broader economic weakness, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns despite high HOUST levels in a late-cycle expansion, or if the Rank IC for this mechanism is below 0.05 in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is low but payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth is weak, it may indicate labor market tightness without corresponding wage growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns despite low UNRATE and weak PAYEMS growth, or if the Rank IC for this mechanism is below 0.03 in out-of-sample tests.
